description: A four-panel composite figure of Charpy V-notch impact-energy transition curves for Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.9C steel at two silicon levels (1.07 and 1.56 wt.% Si) and two aging times (12 h and 30 h) at 530 °C. All four panels share identical axes: "Energy, Joules" on y (0-100, labelled gridlines every 20 J) versus "Temperature, Celsius" on x (-50 to 30, ticks every 10 °C). Every datum is a single symbol carrying a large vertical error bar, and a smooth S-shaped transition curve is fitted through each set. (a) red circles, "1.07% Si aged 12hrs": values rise from about the 40 J gridline at -40 °C, dip near -30 °C, then climb above the 90 J level at 25 °C. (b) blue diamonds, "1.56% Si aged 12 hrs": the whole curve is displaced downward, from about 20 J at -40 °C to roughly the 70 J level at 25 °C. (c) red circles, "1.07 Si aged 30hrs": intermediate, from about 20 J at -40 °C to just under 60 J at 25 °C. (d) blue diamonds, "1.56% Si aged 30 hrs": the lowest curve, from about 12 J at -40 °C to the mid-30s of joules at 25 °C. Together the panels show that both higher Si and longer aging at 530 °C lower the transition curve and reduce upper-shelf impact energy. No numeric data labels are printed; values are readable only against the 20 J gridlines.

subfigures.description: Charpy impact energy vs temperature (J vs °C, y 0-100, x -50 to 30) for red-circle data labelled "1.07% Si aged 12hrs"; points near the 40 J line at -40 °C rise through the mid-range to above the 90 J level at 25 °C, each with a vertical error bar, plus a smooth S-shaped fit.

Same axes and symbol style, blue diamonds labelled "1.56% Si aged 12 hrs"; the curve is shifted to lower energy, roughly 20 J at -40 °C rising to about the 70 J level at 25 °C, with large error bars especially near 0 and 25 °C.
Same axes, red circles labelled "1.07 Si aged 30hrs"; energies lie between panels (a) and (d), from about 20 J at -40 °C to just below 60 J at 25 °C, with a flat region around -20 to 0 °C.
Same axes, blue diamonds labelled "1.56% Si aged 30 hrs"; this is the lowest curve of the group, from about 12 J at -40 °C to the mid-30s of joules at 25 °C, with wide error bars at the upper end.

observations.observation: All four panels plot the same axes: y = "Energy, Joules" from 0 to 100 with labelled gridlines at 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100, and x = "Temperature, Celsius" from -50 to 30 with ticks every 10 °C.
Panels (a) and (c) use red circles and are labelled "1.07% Si" (a: aged 12hrs, c: aged 30hrs); panels (b) and (d) use blue diamonds and are labelled "1.56% Si" (b: aged 12 hrs, d: aged 30 hrs).
Every data point in all four panels carries a vertical error bar; the bars are largest at the high-temperature end of each curve.
A smooth S-shaped transition curve is fitted to each data set, rising monotonically from a low-temperature plateau to a high-temperature plateau.
At the highest testing temperature (~25 °C) the curves rank from highest to lowest energy in the order (a) 1.07% Si 12 h > (b) 1.56% Si 12 h > (c) 1.07% Si 30 h > (d) 1.56% Si 30 h.
Panel (a) shows a local minimum near -30 °C before the curve rises with temperature; the other three panels rise without such a pronounced dip.
No numeric values are printed next to any data point or curve; the only exact numbers visible are the axis tick labels and the panel annotations of Si content and aging time.
The caption states the breaking energy decreases for all temperatures and aging conditions as the silicon amount increases.
The caption states increased κ-carbide (j-carbide) precipitation dramatically decreases impact energy for both silicon levels.
The citing text states room-temperature breaking energy fell from 93 J to 68 J in 12-h aged samples and from 58 J to 35 J in 30-h aged samples on increasing Si.

The citing text states that lowering the testing temperature to -40 °C sharply reduced notch toughness, with increasing silicon lowering the breaking energy by an average of 15 J for samples aged 12 h.
The citing text states that at 30 h of aging the difference in -40 °C breaking energy was statistically the same regardless of silicon content.
The citing text states the specimens were aged in the range 300-352 BHN and had low phosphorus (<0.003% P).
